One is run in Washington by Rubio's former Senate chief of staff and counts Wiles' daughter as a partner. The other is Wiles' old firm. Anthropic has paid the two $1.63 million since April 2025. The first is Continental Strategy, which Anthropic has paid $740,000 since April 2025. Its Washington managing partner, Alberto Martinez, is named on all six of Continental's quarterly reports for the AI lab. Meanwhile, Continental's report for April through June lists the National Security Council (NSC) among the offices it lobbied, and its report for July through September lists the State Department. Rubio is both national security adviser and secretary of state. Anthropic hired Ballard Partners on March 9, four days after the Pentagon labeled the company a supply-chain risk, Bloomberg reported. Wiles was a managing partner there until 2019. Ballard's first report, covering the rest of March, lists the White House Office and the Executive Office of the President. Ballard's report for April through June adds the NSC as well , and Anthropic has paid the firm $890,000 this year. Rubio's memo, dated March 30, went to a handful of Cabinet secretaries ahead of Trump's May trip to China, according to the New York Times . Rubio wrote it from a CIA report, recasting the agency's findings "in his own more assertive terms," the Washington Post reported Friday, though CIA officials aren't convinced Alice Huang - the Chinese national at the center of Jensen Huang's ouster - knowingly passed anything to Beijing. Huang tried at least three times to get a meeting with Rubio and never got one , two people familiar with the matter told the Washington Sun . Rubio's aides nixed proposed talks in the spring of 2025, again that summer and again early this year, with his office saying he was booked or couldn't accommodate the Nvidia chief. The snubs deepened fears inside Nvidia that powerful forces in the US government were out to undermine Huang's influence as a leading voice for closer economic ties with Beijing, the Sun reported. Huang was Washington's loudest corporate backer of open-weight models , the cheap alternative to the closed systems Anthropic sells, and his exit clears the way for a crackdown on them. David Sacks argued on All-In that the ouster served Anthropic's "safetyist" allies, and physicist Steve Hsu wrote that he had heard Nvidia was planning "to go hard at producing frontier class open models" so it wouldn't depend on OpenAI or Anthropic. Under Huang, Nvidia built its own family of open models, Nemotron, backed startups including Reflection AI, Thinking Machines Lab and Poolside, and was moving to acquire Hugging Face. " Nvidia was on a titanic collision course with the labs ," the CEO of a leading AI startup told Business Insider , and Replit CEO Amjad Masad called the ouster an attack on open models at a conference Monday. Meanwhile, Trump said Monday he doesn't know that Alice Huang was a spy "at all," and defended Lutnick. He called Huang a "legend" after the resignation, and Huang was reportedly weighing a comeback as his Silicon Valley allies lean on Nvidia's board - which isn't considering it , the FT reported. By the third quarter Ballard's brief had widened from Pentagon procurement to "US policy regarding AI," and its report adds the Pentagon and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, with the NSC still on the list. Two of the five Ballard lobbyists on that report came straight out of the national security apparatus. Amaryllis Fox Kennedy is listed as a CIA clandestine service officer from 2003 to 2009 and a deputy director of national intelligence in 2025 and 2026. Micah Ketchel, on the account since March, is listed as Rep. Mike Waltz's chief of staff from 2019 to 2025, then a senior adviser to the national security adviser and at the State Department. Continental promoted Katie Wiles days after the 2024 election, around the time it brought in Martinez. She is not a registered lobbyist and isn't named on the firm's reports for Anthropic. A White House official told CBS last month that Susie Wiles doesn't discuss work with her daughters. On April 17, Wiles hosted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at the White House with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent , a meeting the White House called "productive and constructive." Wiles was out as chief of staff on Nov. 6, and has since faced "pay-for-play" accusations from former Kennedy adviser Calley Means centered on Ballard (however he incorrectly accused them of representing Pfizer). Brian Ballard says the firm's dealings with her as chief of staff "have been limited and have been the exception, not the rule." Wiles could face a House probe once Democrats take over next year , Rep. Robert Garcia said last week, and her successor, Stephen Miller, has tightened the rules on White House staff meeting lobbyists. Bessent said Sunday that Nvidia needs a "dramatic shakeup" and should go outside for Huang's successor. He reportedly confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick in the Situation Room over why Megaspeed isn't blacklisted, and later pinned the failure on Commerce on CNBC. Commerce and the Justice Department put out a joint statement Monday night to address what they called "inaccurate information circulating in public reporting." It says Commerce opened an export-control investigation into Megaspeed in 2024, after its monitoring for chip diversion turned up suspicious activity, and that its investigators asked Nvidia in May 2025 for records of direct or indirect sales to the company. Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in June 2025 , according to the statement, the same month Commerce agents and Singaporean law enforcement made an on-site check at Megaspeed and interviewed its CEO, Alice Huang. The Justice Department then took the lead on a criminal investigation. The New York Times reported last week that Commerce's probe was halted late last year after Nvidia's general counsel reached out to the agents running it. In the third quarter Continental added Caroline Farr, listed as a former senior adviser at the Treasury Department, to the account. Commerce, which put export controls on Anthropic's top models in June and lifted them June 30, is on three. On Monday, Commerce closed the loophole that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia chips in data centers outside China. The rule was "written by and at the direction" of Treasury and the National Security Council , the Washington Sun reported. Business Insider called it a major win for Amodei, who has pushed harder than almost anyone for strict limits on chip sales to China. Anthropic's own third-quarter disclosure , which reports $2.11 million in lobbying, names the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act and the MATCH Act , the chip curbs the hawks in Congress want. All three are now attached to the Senate's defense bill, and Sen. Jim Banks told the Post after Huang's exit that he is more hopeful than ever they will pass. Recall that Anthropic has been spending heavily in Washington. Its federal lobbying came to $3.13 million in 2025 and $5.64 million in the first half of 2026 alone. Anthropic has also given $40 million to Public First Action, a group pushing AI safeguards and chip export controls. Meanwhile, the memo grew out of electronic surveillance of Alice Huang that had been running for well over a year, and Trump was first briefed on it late last year, according to the Times, months before Anthropic hired Ballard for its Pentagon fight. That spring Anthropic also had business of its own before the offices on Continental's reports: the Pentagon blacklisting, its Mythos talks with Treasury and the White House, and the June export controls. Commerce's own investigation of Megaspeed began in 2024, before Anthropic hired either firm, according to Monday's statement. "Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models," Amodei wrote July 27 , in a post that also called for keeping powerful chips out of China and cracking down on smuggling. Nvidia, meanwhile, committed $10 billion to a private placement alongside Anthropic's IPO - which is due to price this week. Huang has been asked to appear before the US House panels on Dec 1, Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, and Lutnick has agreed to testify there Dec. 10. Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter will testify Dec. 2. The next lobbying reports, covering October through December, are due Jan. 20 - and will show whether Anthropic's firms are still working the offices Rubio runs.
